question.problem:
$$
X=[\begin{aligned}7 & 13 & 10 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the observation matrix $X$ above, where the individual observations are given in columns. Find the sample covariance matrix of the data.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that  the sample covariance matrix is given by

$$
C=\frac{1}{n-1}B{B}^{T},
$$

where $B$ is the observation matrix in the mean-deviation form, and $n$ is the number of observations.

So, we first need to compute the mean-deviation form of our observation matrix.

The sample mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{1}{3}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}([\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}30 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{1} & ={x}_{1}-m=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {b}_{2} & ={x}_{2}-m=[\begin{aligned}13 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {b}_{3} & ={x}_{3}-m=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 0\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,  the mean-deviation form is

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, the sample covariance matrix is 

$$
\begin{aligned}C & =\frac{1}{3-1}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 3 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}18 & -3 \\ -3 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
